title: Enhancing Caries Protection during First Molar Eruption: A Split Mouth Study on Sealant Effectiveness.
summary: When the first permanent molars come through a child’s gums, they are especially at risk of developing tooth decay because this process can take up to two years and the teeth are often only partly visible during this time. As a result, children find these teeth difficult to clean properly, and toothbrush bristles often cannot reach the deep grooves on the chewing surfaces where food and bacteria can collect. To protect these vulnerable teeth, dentists commonly place a thin protective coating into the grooves. There are different types of these protective coatings: one type is plastic-based and must be applied to a completely dry tooth, while another type is cement-based, releases fluoride, and can be used even when the tooth is slightly wet, which may be helpful while the tooth is still erupting. The purpose of this study is to find out which of these two materials provides better protection against tooth decay and stays in place longer during the eruption phase of the first permanent molars, and which one is easier and more comfortable to use during routine dental care. In this study, children with erupting first permanent molars will receive both types of protective coatings, with one material placed on a molar on one side of the mouth and the other material placed on the matching molar on the opposite side, with the choice of side decided by chance so that a direct comparison can be made under the same conditions. The child’s comfort and cooperation during treatment, as well as the dentist’s experience applying each material, will be recorded, and parents will be asked about their child’s reaction and overall satisfaction. The treated teeth will be checked again after six months, one year, and two years to see how well the coatings remain in place and whether any new tooth decay has developed, with the overall goal of identifying the most effective and child-friendly way to protect newly erupting permanent molars.
conditions: Caries prevention during eruption of first permanent molars

interventions.name:
Arm 1 –  Helioseal F Plus® (Resin-Based Sealant)

Each child receives Helioseal F Plus® (Ivoclar Vivadent) on one first permanent molar. The resin-based sealant is applied under dry conditions following etching, rinsing, and light-curing according to manufacturer instructions.

Arm 2 – Ketac™ Universal (Glass Ionomer Sealant) 
The contralateral molar in the same child is sealed with Ketac™ Universal (3M), a conventional glass ionomer cement that can be applied under moist conditions without etching or light-curing.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children aged 5 to 8 years.

Presence of at least two contralateral erupting first permanent molars suitable for fissure sealing.

Good general health and cooperative behavior suitable for dental treatment.

Written informed consent obtained from parents or legal guardians.
Exclusion criteria:
Systemic or chronic diseases that may affect oral health or dental development.

Teeth with existing carious lesions, restorations, or developmental enamel defects.

Uncooperative behavior preventing proper isolation or sealant application.

Allergy or known intolerance to any component of the sealant materials.

Children who have participated in another clinical study within the last 30 days.
